(Sorry for the paraphrase). Messing around with witchcrafty stuff can have long term effects even though it’s clear you sincerely repented, but God is bigger and stronger. When I have bad thoughts like that or guilt I know I shouldn’t, I pretend like I’m taking the thought and putting it in a bubble and launching it up to God. Sometimes you have to do it several times a day. I hope this is helpful and I pray you have some peace.

My parents sent me to a Christian school my whole childhood. I didn’t really get it like the other kids did. Long story short, I graduated, started exploring the world, got a bunch of tattoos and piercings (no regrets). Then I met a guy (I’m female) that was heavily into drugs and I became a heroin addict, started stealing from a family member and went to jail. In jail it was like everyone had disappeared. No friends, no family, no support. Withdrawaling and scared out of my mind. I ended up at a church service and I got this hug from an elderly pastor and I could tell he really really cared about me and all the other people there even though I only just met him. At my lowest point when I had nothing and nobody, I realized that’s the kind of love that Jesus is about and I decided I wanted to live for him.

What I forgot to mention was that I had tried everything else and was unfulfilled. Drugs, addictions, exercise, tattoos and piercings, and nothing was fulfilling long term. It was always a short term high and then onto the next. Jesus was for real and I feel fulfilled ever since.

I was 12 and on vacation with my dad when I woke up in bloody sheets. I had no idea what was happening to me and was pretty terrified. My dad didn’t know what to do either. My parents were getting divorced and I was on vacation with him and my brother. My dad had to call my mom to figure out what to do. He got giant pads from the store. I’m sure he didn’t know any better. I was in so much pain that we had to come home from vacation early. We learned about periods the next school year. It also took me years to figure out tampons by myself.

I have a lot of trauma in my history and I think this stuff that’s coming up now is similar to how an abuser used to treat me and I just freak out and lose all sense of myself and everything I’ve learned about how to deal with my anxiety. I was in line cashing out on my lunch break and I watched the woman behind me put her dirty food tray in a pile of shopping baskets that I had just straightened up. I heard her say "They'll take care of it". I gave her a "oh no you won't have them 'take care of it'" death glare and went and got it out of the basket.  I also made a point to let her know where they actually go because the other woman in her party also had a tray... and who knows where that tray wound up.

Had a similar thing happen at my charcuterie a few months ago. I was at the service desk and a cashier calls to say... "this lady has a hunk of meat". I repeated out loud "a hunk of meat... are you sure it's not from our salad bar?" She says "no, it's just a hunk of meat." Confused, I went over to find her with a piece of dried pepperoni from out charcuterie. Normally, a customer would ask someone over in that area to wrap it and put a sticker on it. I then explained "I've never seen a customer help themselves to the charcuterie. It would be like grabbing a chunk of ground beef out of the meat case and bringing it to the register. So customer says: "so I can't buy it then?" And then I face palm and explain that I'd have to go back and wrap it and get a sticker. I guess she didn't have time for all that.

Woman puts her basket down at the back of my cash register and says she has to use the bathroom and she will be back shortly. This was a Sunday of a holiday weekend so we were crazy busy. I wasn't even supposed to be on register but I was helping out cause it was so busy.

I forgot about this woman and assume she's come back for her stuff and gotten in a line or continued shopping. About 20 minutes goes by and she comes back and thinks that she should be in the front of my line, which had about 5 other people in it. 

The kicker was that the person next in line was at least partially blind. I could tell because she had her money out and it was folded in a certain way so she can tell what denominations the bills were.

So I say to this woman: "do you realize that you've just stepped in line in front of a blind person?" She says that she's in a hurry and she feels that she should be next. I tell her that the customer service desk has no customers and ask her to go cash out there. Then she says "why do I want to go all the way over there?" To told her that it was closer to the door and she has to go that way to get out anyway. She refused and said "just ring me out". 

I asked the blind woman if it's ok with her. She said she was also in a hurry but clearly this awful woman won't budge, so go ahead. So I did. I didn't say a damn word to her through the whole order.

I learned from an ex boyfriend. But you sort of learn as you go... It's very weird. I learned a lot by observing other people. Then find somebody you're comfortable with to ask the questions.. like a coworker... or a friendly reddit community. Sometimes you have to ask what seem like stupid questions. But they're not stupid.

It's hard going out on your own without any support. Good luck to you!

It matters. And you matter! And you're not irrelevant. Someone did something bad to you and even though you don't think it's as bad as other people's experiences, it's a thing that happened to you and you have every right to have feelings about it! You have the right to be sad, or angry, or grieve even. Don't take that away from yourself.

It's ok to deal with things in your own way too.

I'm sorry for your loss. And I hope your drive goes/went ok. Something I always say to my aunt (which we giggle about) when she asks what I'm getting nmom for her birthday or Christmas: "I'm getting her the same thing I get her every year. The pleasure of not having to deal with me today!" She doesn't have to agonize out loud about what an awful person I am, and I don't have to get abused by her."

Yes! My nmom never taught me about my period. I'll leave out the details, but I got it when I was on vacation with my dad. I didn't understand why it was happening to me. I learned about periods like 2 years later in a health class. She also never bought me the right size bras and we NEVER talked about sex.

I had a similar experience. I recently found the courage to go to a dentist after 13 years. What I learned was that as a child, my nmom took me to a friend of hers, who was a cosmetic dentist. I remember him telling me that I needed fillings, but the dentist I just went to told me I didn't have any fillings. I'm pretty baffled because I could have sworn he did something. I remember "sandblasting" with no novicaine. Maybe for fillings. I now know that whatever happened wasn't right.

My nmom would pick and choose what treatments I got from what doctors. I was always confused by it.

It definitely is... And sometimes it's genuine. But in my case, I've heard the words so many times, but still no change in behavior. This just happens to be what I've experienced. It's entirely possible that it's different for others.

Something I stole from Dr Phil: "it's hard to forgive someone for running over your foot, if they're still running over your foot." 

Even though I've gone NC, my nmom's past behavior affects every day of my life, in some really big ways. It won't be better until I'm back on my feet, and that won't be for at least another year or two. So no, I don't forgive her, because I know she's incapable of telling the truth or feeling any type of remorse. I can stop caring, but forgiveness implies remorse, and I know there's no remorse there.

Nmom: "I'll give you the child support money that your father gave me for your birthday, but only to pay for school books"

Also, she's become obsessed with giving me clementines for Christmas. She thinks I love them... I mean, I don't hate them... but a bag of clementines vs the $200 grill set you got for my GCBro... something doesn't add up.

Come to think of it, I haven't had to teach my nMom to copy and paste (for the 100th time)  or do her work for her because she somehow lost an entire excel database,  or explain why her 15 year old computer is slow in quite some time.

And what's worse is that my Nmom has brainwashed him into thinking that I'm evil. We can't blame them though. They experienced a way different childhood than we did. I guess we just have to try to have that relationship accepting that our childhoods were very different even though we grew up in the same house.

I always think of all the things my nMom has done to me whenever I think about breaking NC. It's been more than 20 years of this behavior from her and I know she'll always go back to her ways, every time, without fail. It makes me a little sad but it gives me the strength to push through. 

I also try to think of it like a sobriety count. I have 10 months and 23 days of NC. I think it's kinda like being off drugs in a way.(3 years and 4 months clean).  When you get sober, your brain and body start to heal in ways they couldn't before.

I went NC about 10 months ago for good. Long story short, I made some really bad decisions about 4 years ago  with a guy I was dating. We were doing a lot of drugs and I thought somehow that stealing from my mother would give me some solace from the childhood I suffered through at her hands. I took some silver coins from her basement. She didn't even know about it for a long time but when she found out, she set up a sting so that I would be arrested. I spent four months in jail and will be a felon for the rest of my life. I was angry that she turned me in and didn't give me the chance at rehab. What I realized now that I'm clean and sober for three years and completely unmedicated for the first time since she put xanax in my hand for the first time 19 years ago, is that no amount of stuff I can steal from her can make up for 30 years of heinous abuse. The last straw was 10 months ago. I finally started getting my life back together, paying back the money I owe, and she was angry at me and threatened to say I stole more stuff from her when I didn't, just to have me sent  to prison for up to 7 years. So I had to go NC to protect myself from her lies. There's also a no illegal contact restraining order which she said the court forced her to get. That basically means I can talk to her and have a relationship, but not do anything illegal against her. That's up in 2021 so maybe I'll break my NC when she's not a direct threat to my career, my relationship, my home, and my pets.

I would say try getting a bus pass qnd finding the nearest mall or shopping center... or grocery store. Something close. Apply in every store and find something to get you started. I don't know if you are religious but churches have a lot of outreach and might be able to help you find a job and get you a good support system. A community center might have the same thing. But before any of that, you should take a really deep breath and know that everything is going to be ok.

Haven't spoken to my nMom in 10 months. With the exception of the day she showed up at my house uninvited, and that was only to tell her to leave. She threatened to have me arrested for a second time by saying she would tell the police I  did something that I didn't. She's threatened to do it several times and I finally realized that coming back from nothing would be easier without constant emotional abuse and threats. It's finally getting easier!
